proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 47 prints /cʰiulə/ “touched” as an /iu/ diphthong example; p. 73 identifies -lə as the past marker. Turner5055 gives Oriya cʰũibā and OAwadhi chuvaï “touches,” beside Nepali chunu; the Darai cʰiu- stem and past inflection fit this family.

proposals.evidence: Dhakal p. 54 prints /cʰike/ “to touch” among aspirated affricates, distinct from unaspirated /cirike/ “to split.” Turner5055 gives Nepali chunu, Maithili chūyab and Hindi chūnā “touches”; Darai cʰi- is the same touch stem.
